basis: Neurodevelopmental impairment defines syndrome; skeletal malformations and gonadal insufficiency each occur in 80-99%; recurrent infections alone do not establish immunodeficiency.

decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: radioulnar synostosis, elbow abnormalities and scoliosis occur in 80-99%; associated skeletal lesions rather than the defining neurodevelopmental phenotype.

basis: Bardet-Biedl phenotype: retinal dystrophy, obesity and renal anomalies are major criteria; cognitive impairment affects ~50-60%; common polydactyly omitted at cap.

decisions.renal: primary: renal structural or functional abnormalities are a major Bardet-Biedl diagnostic criterion; this BBS10 umbrella predominantly represents that phenotype.

basis: Unresolved gene/protein-like legacy entry without a disease phenotype; no organ assignment is defensible from 'tubulin, beta' alone.

decisions.neurologic: none: neither definition nor ancestors supply a neurologic phenotype; a tubulin name alone cannot establish neurologic disease.

basis: Tumor originates in pancreatic endocrine delta cells; digestive symptoms reflect hormonal inhibition without established gastrointestinal tissue damage; gallbladder disease is separate.

decisions.gastrointestinal: none: diarrhea, steatorrhea and hypochlorhydria reflect hormone-mediated suppression; they do not establish direct intestinal or exocrine pancreatic damage.

basis: Corneal sensory loss and degeneration define keratopathy; fifth-nerve abnormalities (80-99%) describe antecedent denervation, not additional neurologic injury caused by the corneal disease.

decisions.neurologic: none: trigeminal dysfunction is the cause of corneal degeneration; the keratopathy does not itself produce a separate cranial neuropathy despite the 80-99% HPO association.

basis: Autoimmune cutaneous disease without clinical myositis; ILD occurred in ~13% in a broad historical review, with higher rates in selected anti-MDA5 and Asian cohorts.

decisions.pulmonary: none: ILD is ~13% in a broad historical review; higher rates in selected cohorts do not establish >=30% across amyopathic dermatomyositis.

basis: Severe Zellweger metabolic disease has defining CNS and liver dysfunction; damaging ocular disease occurs in >30%; characteristic skeletal stippling omitted at the four-axis cap.

decisions.hepatic: primary: hepatic dysfunction, supported by jaundice, hepatomegaly and elevated AST, is a core diagnostic manifestation of severe Zellweger disease.
decisions.neurologic: primary: severe developmental impairment, neonatal hypotonia and seizures constitute the defining CNS phenotype of classic Zellweger disease.
decisions.ocular: involved: cataract and retinal disease cause visual impairment commonly (>30%) in severe Zellweger disease; cataract is recorded here.
decisions.musculoskeletal: none: characteristic epiphyseal stippling has less functional burden than the retained CNS, liver and ocular disease; omitted at the four-axis cap.

basis: Peroxisomal metabolic disorder; neurologic dysfunction affects most, hepatopathy >30% and hearing loss most; common retinal disease omitted at the four-axis cap.

decisions.hepatic: involved: hepatopathy commonly exceeds 30% across Zellweger spectrum; severity varies across PEX13 subtypes.
decisions.neurologic: involved: developmental or progressive neurologic dysfunction affects most across the spectrum; the peroxisomal metabolic defect defines this umbrella.
decisions.ocular: none: retinal degeneration is common (>30%), but hearing loss is more frequent and retained at the four-axis cap.
decisions.otologic: involved: sensorineural hearing loss affects most Zellweger-spectrum patients and causes substantial functional loss.

basis: Renal acidification failure, acidosis and hereditary hemolysis define disease; rickets frequency is unquantified here and not established at >=30%.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: rickets is variable, not a defining criterion, and a >=30% frequency is not established for this subtype.

basis: Aortic and skeletal disease characterize this group; Marfan predominates, with ectopia lentis in ~60%, supporting ocular damage in >=30% of patients across the umbrella.

decisions.ocular: involved: Marfan is the predominant subtype and ectopia lentis affects ~60% of Marfan patients; patient-weighted frequency plausibly exceeds 30% across this group.
